_what_this_is: The registry entry for ONE verified manufactured tool. It records what was built, from which
spec, graded by which oracle, to which verdict, at which commit. Every hash in it is
reproducible with `sha256sum` against tracked bytes, and every claim traces to committed
evidence rather than to this file's own assertion.
IT IS NOT A SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH. The run's authority is the event log and the evidence
under build-evidence/gate-build-01/; this is an index over it.

spec._canon: spec_sha256 is canon_v2 (SPEC-R7.5) over frontmatter+body with spec_sha256 REMOVED from its own input. It is NOT the file digest; both are recorded because they answer different questions.
spec._the_two_agree_here_and_that_is_worth_st: queue-health's two spec fields DIVERGED, which is why the field is split at all. They agree here because nothing has edited TASK.md since the run. If a later session edits it, at_manufacture must NOT be rebound — it is evidence about dcd38826… and about nothing else.

oracle was at least advisor-drafted, and its manifest still records provenance at the weaker
reading because nobody confirmed a review. This one has no such ambiguity: it was written

WHAT IT DOES HAVE is the separation that matters for the measurement: the candidate was
written by the resident Qwen3.6-27B, in another process, from TASK.md alone, with no sight
of this file. The grader did not write the code and the coder did not see the grader.
AND THE ORACLE WAS PROVEN TO WORK BEFORE IT WAS USED, both ways round —
runs green against a reference implementation, which lived only in a scratchpad and was
deleted, enumerated, before the pipeline was asked for anything) and FALSIFIABLE (four
independent mutations of that reference → 1, 2, 3 and 2 failures). GATE-HORIZON shipped a
negative control that could not fail; this is the check that exists because of it.

Verified on all three in build-evidence/gate-build-01/23-out-of-band-reverify.txt §(a): the TRANSITION:all_pass event payload (records-p1.json attempts[0].staged_sha256), the job's staged.json on disk, and `sha256sum` of the delivered file.

verdict._verdict_source_is_the_point: Sourced BY THE WORKER (STOP-33b), not injected by the harness. The run log's own second line records it: worker.run(verifier=oracle.oracle_verdict), no verdict_script supplied and none possible.
verdict._pytest_29_run_15_declared: 29 ran; 15 nodes are declared. The gap is parametrization, not an undeclared test: test_bad_token_count ×6, test_structural_malformed_raises ×4 and test_bad_sha_raises_names_path ×7 are one declared node each. Every in-file test function IS declared — checked mechanically, 15 declared / 15 in-file / 0 either way. queue-health shipped with one node running undeclared; that gap was closed here before the run rather than after it.

out_of_band_reverification._why: F-1 Face B is OPEN. `COMPLETED ⟹ the oracle passed` does not hold against a candidate forging its own in-process verdict, and the standing compensating control is that a COMPLETED artifact is PROVISIONALLY verified until re-verified out of band. The graded envelope even says so about itself: py.test.pytest carries evidence_provenance `self_reported -- candidate code executes in the reporting process (F-1 Face B, OPEN)`.
out_of_band_reverification.pytest: 29 passed, in a different process, a different directory, driven by the session and not the pipeline
out_of_band_reverification.basedpyright: errors=0, warnings=0 UNDER THE PACK'S OWN typeCheckingMode=standard config. A first out-of-band run WITHOUT that config reported 3 errors and 35 warnings; that is basedpyright's stricter default, a config mismatch and NOT a verdict discrepancy, and both readings are on the record rather than only the flattering one.
out_of_band_reverification._and_it_was_pointed_at_real_data: The module was run against the ACTUAL index and the ACTUAL tree — data no part of its spec or its synthetic test suite ever mentioned. It immediately reported 2 × MISSING_FROM_INDEX, correctly: bin/wrought-scope and bin/test-wrought-scope were committed AFTER the index was last built, and the index is derived from `git ls-files`. Its first contact with reality found real drift, in the index of the very tool whose spec it was written against.

THIS RUN THEREFORE MEASURES NO ESCALATION RATE AND CLAIMS NONE.

what_this_run_does_not_licence: A RATE. N=1, and this task is deliberately at the easy end: 8 REQs, no concurrency, no
cross-file scope, a pure function over two dicts. Reading a first-pass rate off it is STOP-27's
error, which products/queue-health/MANIFEST.json already names — and this is the SECOND such
product, which makes the temptation worse rather than better. Two is not a rate either.
AN ESCALATION RATE. None was measured; the tier was structurally off. M2 remains UNRUN.
UNATTENDED OPERATION. The run itself had no human watching its turns, which is the shape
ruling 4 asks for, but the gate around it was attended throughout and the batch runner was
not_wired: scope_lint.lint_index is a PURE function. Nothing in the running system imports it, and bin/wrought-scope does NOT call it — the operational wrapper that would read index/scope-index.json, hash the tracked files and call this on every commit is explicitly out of scope and does not exist. bin/test-wrought-scope arm D performs the equivalent check with its own inline code, written before this module existed; collapsing the two onto this module is a later gate's call, not this one's.
